clue.text: Nag guide to be shown round ruined chapels to the east

indicators.note: the guide's word is taken round the other letters, as a visitor is shown round a building

parts.note: to guide is to steer

indicators.note: ruined chapels are knocked into a new shape, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tour guide leads visitors round some tumbledown chapels in the east of a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' looks like a verb but is the horse; a steeplechaser is a horse that runs races over fences.
explanation.definitionFit: A nag is a horse, often a tired old one, and a steeplechaser is a racehorse trained for jumps.

clue.text: He treats this part differently, including the finale

indicators.note: the letters of these words are set out differently, a signal to rearrange them
the anagram takes in the extra letter as well as the two words

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the finale of a word is its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone instructs an actor to play this scene another way, finale and all.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like stage direction, but 'He treats' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist is a practitioner who treats patients, so 'he treats' describes the job.

clue.text: It happens on occasion

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a happening, something that takes place
second meaning: a special function or gathering

explanation.walkthrough: 'On occasion' reads as 'sometimes', but 'occasion' is a definition on its own and 'on' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is anything that takes place, and also a planned social function such as a party.

clue.text: Seating space set up next to one's accommodation

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the word from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: jelly sets, or gels
room is accommodation, as in 'room and board'

explanation.surface: Arranging a lodging where everything is set up next door.
explanation.definitionFit: Legroom is the space in front of a seat for a passenger's legs.

clue.text: Mean to be cautious

definitions.meaning: second meaning: taking care to avoid risk

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean to be' reads as 'intend to be', but 'Mean' is a definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Being careful with money is a polite way of calling someone stingy, and careful also means wary of danger.

clue.text: Opinions wrongly situated in time

indicators.note: the letter for time goes inside the rearranged letters
the word situated is placed wrongly, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Views that are out of their proper moment in history.
explanation.definitionFit: Attitudes are settled ways of thinking, the stances or views someone holds.

clue.text: Due to go out with old girlfriend before show

indicators.note: the former partner comes before the rest in the answer

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: the word due is sent out of order, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is booked to take a former girlfriend out before a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' looks like a theatre outing but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To exude confidence is to display it plainly, so exude is a synonym of show.

clue.text: Dig up kind of food as suitable ingredient for a stew

parts.note: pigs root, digging up the ground with their snouts
vegetables are a broad class of food

explanation.surface: Unearth a type of food that will go well in a casserole.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrots, turnips and parsnips are root vegetables, classic additions to a stew.

clue.text: Sporting events present difficulty to different types of people

parts.note: a present difficulty, one in the way now, is an obstacle
humanity is divided into races

explanation.surface: Some sports cause problems for certain kinds of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present difficulty' reads as a verb phrase but is a noun phrase: a difficulty that is present.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstacle races are contests in which runners must clear hurdles, nets and walls.

clue.text: Too keen once again? Agree to differ

parts.note: doing something over is doing it once again

indicators.note: the letters of agree are made to differ from their order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An argument where one side presses too hard, until both settle on agreeing to differ.
explanation.definitionFit: Overeager means excessively enthusiastic, a synonym phrase for too keen.

clue.text: It may be a pointer to success or failure

definitions.meaning: sounds like a sign or indicator; literally a digit that points
a raised or lowered digit gives a verdict of approval or rejection

explanation.surface: Something that suggests whether a venture will work.
explanation.walkthrough: Thumbs up means success, thumbs down failure, and the digit points one way or the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The thumb gives the gesture of approval or disapproval by pointing up or down.

clue.text: Characteristic design reflected modern technology

indicators.note: an image reflected in a mirror is reversed, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: design is a form of art
IT, information technology, is modern computing

explanation.surface: A distinctive style of design mirrors present-day technology.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a distinguishing quality or feature, a noun synonym of characteristic.

clue.text: Definitely not in the way

definitions.meaning: seems to mean obstructing, but way here is a road

explanation.surface: Something that is certainly not an obstruction.
explanation.walkthrough: Off-street parking is kept clear of the road, so it is not in the way, the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-street describes something located away from the public road, such as parking.

clue.text: Undemocratic behaviour is off limits to a point

indicators.note: letters that are off are out of place, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Undemocratic conduct is beyond the pale, up to a point.
explanation.definitionFit: Elitism favours a privileged few over the many, the opposite of democratic equality.

clue.text: In dialect turned out to be the same

indicators.note: the words are turned out of their order, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Two words spoken in local dialect proved to mean the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical means exactly alike in every respect, a synonym of the same.

clue.text: Fellow has game against another chap

indicators.note: the game sits next to, against, the second name

parts.note: Ludo is a children's board game played with dice and counters
Vic is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man plays a board game against another man.
explanation.walkthrough: Ludovic is a man's given name, so 'Fellow' defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludovic is a male first name, so it is a fellow in the crossword sense of any man.

clue.text: Girl, upper-class, takes a share without first getting estimate

parts.note: Val is a girl's name
U is the old British label for upper-class usage

indicators.note: the share is taken without its opening letter

parts.note: a ration is a fixed share

explanation.surface: A posh girl claims her portion without first getting a quote.
explanation.definitionFit: A valuation is an assessment of what something is worth, an estimate of its price.

clue.text: The ending is over the top

definitions.meaning: second meaning: excessive, going too far

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a verdict on a melodramatic finale; it is two meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme as a noun is the outermost point, and as an adjective it means excessive or immoderate.

clue.text: Watch the hilltop for one of a pair

parts.note: to eye something is to watch it
the brow of a hill is its top

explanation.surface: Keep a lookout on the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: Faces have two eyebrows, so each is one of a pair.

clue.text: Graduate upset by love's confusion, it's clear

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate

indicators.note: the letters are thrown into confusion, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A graduate is thrown by romantic muddle, and the matter is cleared up.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve is to clear someone of blame or guilt, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Diplomat uttered encouragement to revolutionary

parts.note: 'atta' is a spoken word of encouragement, as in 'atta boy'
Che Guevara is the stock crossword revolutionary

explanation.surface: An envoy cheers on a rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is a junior member of an embassy's diplomatic staff.

clue.text: Separately met fellows at the first property

indicators.note: the pieces meet, joining one after another

parts.note: apart means separately
men are fellows

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some men met individually at the start to view a property.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a flat, a residential unit of property within a building.

clue.text: Hold same view about time to go round

indicators.note: the word for time goes round the word for about

parts.note: an age is a period of time
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Two people share an opinion about when to make another circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to share an opinion, holding the same view as another.

clue.text: Beast of a large number to total up

indicators.note: the letters are totted up, read back from the end, so they are reversed

parts.note: taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
all is the total

explanation.surface: An animal that many people add up.
explanation.definitionFit: A llama is a South American beast of burden related to the camel.

clue.text: Permitted to support a student

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair
taken as written
L is the learner plate on a student driver's car

explanation.surface: Allowed to help out a pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal means permitted by law, the adjective synonym.

clue.text: Song Cyril composed

indicators.note: composed suggests music but also means put together, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Cyril wrote a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric is a song's words, or a short song-like poem.

clue.text: Know about small part turning up in southeast

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a cog is a small part in a machine

indicators.note: turning up makes the little word read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
SE is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone is aware of a minor component appearing in the southeast.
explanation.definitionFit: To recognise someone is to know them on sight, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Sympathy, in the academic sense

parts.note: a fellow is a senior member of a college
feeling is one of the senses, touch

explanation.surface: Fellow-feeling as an academic might understand it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a gloss on the word itself; cryptically it is a college fellow plus a sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellow feeling is sympathy arising from shared experience with another person.
